messages:
alex: FYI saw NaNs in production logs for a single customer on long seqs (8k). looks like paged-attn switched kernels mid-request and softmax blew up :grimacing:

maria: ugh. any repro? can you paste the stack + kernel selection trace? @sam for precision rules

alex: repro attached (small script). root cause looks like a kernel handoff between fused_flash -> paged_fused when kv cache fills a page. snippet of runtime trace:
```
[2026-03-15 14:02:11] kernel_select: chosen=fused_flash (seq=1024)
[2026-03-15 14:02:11] kv_cache: page_boundary hit -> switching to paged_fused
[2026-03-15 14:02:11] fused softmax: max_exp=6.7e38, sum=inf -> output=NaN
```

alex: repro note: only happens when model is using mixed fp8 kernels on the fused path and paged path is bf16 fallback. switching model to bf16 end-to-end removed NaNs. :white_check_mark:

sam: interesting — probably softmax scaling not preserving the same numeric guardrail across kernel implementations. fused_flash was using an fp8-quantized exp approximation without a max-subtraction, paged_fused uses a different exp path. when handoff happens, exponent range can jump.

maria: do we have perf traces for the request? @perf-bot can you dump profiling?

perf-bot: profiling summary (request id r-74c):
- total tokens: 8200
- avg latency before handoff: 12.3ms/token (fused_flash)
- latency after handoff: 18.9ms/token (paged_fused)
- kernel switch idx: 4096 (KV page boundary)
- peak exp values observed (per-token): [1.2e2, 4.6e2, 3.1e38] -> overflow at token 4097

jen: quick thought: we need consistent numeric invariants at kernel boundaries. options:
- ensure both kernels apply log-sum-exp max subtraction (cheap)
- enforce dtype homogenization during page handoff (force bf16 across both)
- add a small exponent clamp on fp8 paths as a safety net

sam: agree. the cleanest is LSE subtraction parity. the fp8 exp approximation we use (fast-approx-exp8) doesn't support dynamic offset well; adding max-subtract to the approximation is tricky but doable. fallback is to cast the softmax accumulator to fp32 for reduction then rescale back which is slightly slower.

maria: perf budget? if we cast to fp32 on the boundary reduce step, how much hit?

perf-bot: quick microbench (attn softmax reduce):
- pure fp8 approx: 0.65ms
- fp8 w/ max-subtract in fp8 path: 0.82ms (est, needs correctness tests)
- fp8 reduce via fp32 accumulator: 1.6ms

alex: customer prefers stability over the small tail latency increase. but we should avoid 2x hit. 0.82ms looks reasonable if it fixes it.

sam: i'll prototype adding explicit max subtract into the approx-exp kernel and add tests that force handoffs at page boundaries. test matrix: seq lengths [4096, 8192], dtypes [fp16, bf16, fp8], kernel combo permutations.

jen: also add a unit that fuzzes exponent ranges to confirm no NaNs. make it part of nightly regression suite. put a perf flag to opt into the fast path once validated.

maria: create a short mitigation for rollout: detect NaN output and route subsequent tokens in that request to bf16 paged path (hot-patch at routing layer). cheap and immediate.

alex: noted. i'll open a hotfix PR for the routing guard and a follow-up PR for the kernel LSE parity change. tagging this as P0 for the runtime team. :exclamation:

sam: thanks. will sync with research tomorrow to confirm approximation math. adding TODOs in the ticket.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime/hotfix/softmax-guardrail -> canary group alpha (3 nodes). ETA 10m.

maria: thanks everyone. please paste PR links here when ready. will update customer and keep monitoring. :eyes:
